messages:
ryan: hi all — first week. building runtime in a docker dev container but runtime process fails immediately with `libcuda.so.1` missing. any ideas?

ryan: run output when launching built binary inside container:
```
./build/bin/runtime: error while loading shared libraries: libcuda.so.1: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

ryan: host has drivers installed (nvidia-smi works on host). inside container `nvidia-smi` prints: `NVIDIA-SMI has failed because it couldn't communicate with the NVIDIA driver.`

natanael: welcome! sounds like the container isn't using the NVIDIA runtime to expose the host driver libs. are you running the container with `--gpus` or the nvidia runtime?

ryan: i started container like `docker run -it --rm -v $PWD:/src redwood/dev-runtime:2025-04 bash` — no `--gpus` flag. thought mounting /usr/local/cuda would be enough.

mika: mounting /usr/local/cuda only gives you toolkit files, not the host's libcuda driver. libcuda is provided by the kernel driver and must be exposed into the container via nvidia-container-toolkit or the old nvidia-docker2 runtime.

devopsbot: CI/dev tip: For local GPU workloads, run with `--gpus all` or use the nvidia runtime in docker-compose. Example: `docker run --gpus all -it --rm -v $PWD:/src redwood/dev-runtime:2025-04 bash`. Ensure `nvidia-container-toolkit` is installed on the host and Docker daemon configured. See https://docs.nvidia.com/datacenter/cloud-native/container-toolkit/install-guide.html

rosie: if you want the container to both compile and run GPU tests, prefer using the official dev image and run it with `--gpus all`. Also avoid bind-mounting host /usr/lib/nvidia* unless you really know the compatibility. It can cause mismatches.

ryan: installed `nvidia-container-toolkit` and restarted docker, then ran with `--gpus all`. `nvidia-smi` inside container now shows GPUs. re-ran the binary and now it errors further with `cudaErrorInitializationError` at runtime init. stack trace points to missing permissions for /dev/nvidiactl.

natanael: check that your user can access the device nodes (usually owned by root:nvidia). Common fix: add your user to the `docker` group (so docker can create devices) and ensure `--privileged` is not required. On some distros udev rules create /dev/nvidia* with group `video` or `render`; adding your user to that group can help when using tools directly on host.

ryan: added user to video group, restarted session. binary starts and GPU smoke tests pass 3/3. nice!

mika: sweet. quick onboarding notes to add: 1) don't just mount /usr/local/cuda — you need nvidia runtime to expose driver libs, 2) use `--gpus all` or the nvidia runtime in compose, 3) prefer official dev images (redwood/dev-runtime) for toolchain parity, 4) check device node permissions if you hit initialization errors.

ryan: added a short doc in onboarding-notes: `runtime/docker-gpu-setup.md` with commands used. thanks for the pointers :raised_hands: closing thread.
